ceiling_statement: The maximum feasible institutional decision authority under H1-H8 is: every trusted state transition (adoption, release, retraction, override) is admitted by one total, pure, decidable kernel predicate K(state, transition, certificate) evaluated at the single writer seat, where acceptance yields a certificate-carrying, sequence-monotonic transition and EVERY other outcome — including an error inside the gate's own predicates — is a recorded, signed refusal with zero state change (fail-closed totality); authorization validity is offline-decidable by any third party recomputing the capability/delegation chain from a committed genesis trust anchor, which no system can eliminate (signatures transfer trust, they cannot create it); machine authority extends exactly to authorization and process compliance, never to the substantive rightness of the institutional decision itself, which remains with the accountable human creator; and absent a real external witness quorum, equivocation resistance is capped at fork consistency — a lying single writer can maintain divergent views, but any two views that ever meet yield producer-attributable cryptographic evidence (two signed checkpoints for the same sequence).
derivation: Four limits. (1) Verification theory: an offline verifier (H8, zero producer trust) can check only decidable predicates over committed bytes; therefore accountable authority is maximized precisely when admission IS a decidable proof-checking problem — certificate-carrying transitions — and cannot exceed it: any 'authority' not reified as a checkable certificate over committed inputs is unverifiable assertion, which H8 rates as zero. (2) Trust-anchor necessity: every signature chain terminates in a key whose bindingness is an axiom (genesis); information-theoretically a verifier with no prior trusted bit can authenticate nothing, so the ceiling is a minimal, committed, explicit genesis anchor — not its elimination. (3) Fail-closed totality (H2+H3): a gate predicate that errors has produced UNKNOWN, and H2 forbids UNKNOWN upgrading to pass; hence the ceiling gate maps every non-proof path to refusal, and — because H6 demands accountability of refusals too — the refusal itself must be a derivation (which article, which conjunct, over which committed facts), durably recorded. Nothing stronger exists: 'never wrongly refuse' would require deciding properties of arbitrary future predicates (Rice's theorem), so the ceiling keeps refusal cheap, recorded, and creator-overridable ONLY via an explicit, reason-carrying, logged override (never silent). (4) Equivocation bound (SUNDR result): with a single writer and no independent witnesses, fork consistency is the provable maximum — clients cannot detect a fork they never compare across; full split-view resistance requires an external cosigning quorum, which is not within unilateral reach today (B0 honestly declares witnesses NIL), so the honest ceiling claim is fork-consistency-with-evidence, not split-view immunity. The 'process not substance' clause follows from H1: judging legal-substantive correctness would put a model in the trusted path; the ceiling system makes the boundary of its own authority a committed, checkable artifact.
attainment_mechanism: All components exist or are directly buildable in the SBCL repo + Ed25519: (1) keep the structural barrier — the CLOS :around method of systems/orchestrator-cli/constitutional-dispatch.lisp already makes it impossible for any registered command to reach its primary method without passing the constitution, with explicit logged --force + LAWMAX_OVERRIDE_REASON override; (2) flip the gate to fail-closed: source/constitutional-gate.lisp lines 44-45 currently map a predicate error to (values t nil) — replace with a refusal carrying the erring rule's identity, satisfying the ceiling's totality clause (a one-seat change eliminating the fail-open class); (3) implement kernel K as a pure SBCL function realizing the conjuncts of authority-v2/kernel/admission-model.sexp over authority-v2/schema/transition-certificate.cddl certificates, with Ed25519 owner-pin/delegation/revocation checking already seated in source/authority-proof-bundle.lisp and strict DER in source/asn1-der.lisp, anchored in authority-v2/genesis/genesis-policy.sexp; (4) every acceptance AND refusal appended to the signed, read-back-durable adoption ledger (source/adoption-decision.lisp with orchestrator.journal:require-durable!), committed all-or-nothing via the AX-11 transaction so rejection-without-state-change holds by construction; (5) offline verifier in the existing recompute-and-compare style (source/authority-evidence-replay.lisp, systems/orchestrator-epistemic/release-spine.lisp) replays the certificate chain from genesis, trusting no declared root; (6) fork-evidence: signed checkpoints per sequence (specified in authority-v2/store/STORAGE-API.sexp and the C2SP wire format under authority-v2/log/) so any cross-view comparison yields attributable double-signing evidence — the maximum available while the external witness quorum remains unreal.
b0_gap: B0 has the structural skeleton but not the ceiling (B0 map AX-12 row): the admission kernel is spec-only with 0/9 theorems discharged — authority-v2/kernel/admission-model.sexp declares :implementation-status :specification-only and T1-T9 all :blocked-toolchain (verified in file); the constitutional gate FAILS OPEN on predicate error (verified: source/constitutional-gate.lisp:44-45, the comment itself labels it fail-open), directly below the ceiling's fail-closed totality and B0's own zero-error law; 'which acts are unconstitutional' is non-proof-carrying policy prose rather than derivations over committed facts; refusals are printed to the terminal, not durably recorded as signed derivations; and the external witness tier is honestly NIL (authority-v2/log/witness-policy.sexp: external_quorum_status disabled, split_view_resistance_claim nil), so today not even the fork-evidence half is operational. Capability closure at the OS layer (the arbitration substrate) is the one part already executionally proven.
lean_obligation: Define State, Transition, Cert, and a genesis-rooted authorization judgment Auth : Chain -> Key -> Prop with decidable checker checkAuth. Define K : State -> Transition -> Cert -> Sum State Refusal, total by construction. Prove: (T1-soundness) K s t c = inl s' -> checkAuth (chain c) (signer c) = true AND all admission conjuncts hold AND seq s' = seq s + 1; (T7-rejection-inert) K s t c = inr r -> the committed store state is unchanged and r carries a derivation naming the failed conjunct over committed inputs; (T-fail-closed) every execution path of K, including exceptional evaluation of any conjunct, terminates in inl or inr — formalized as K total with no partiality-monad escape, and UNKNOWN never coerced to acceptance; (T-verifier-agreement) any two verifiers recomputing from genesis over equal committed logs produce equal accept/reject verdicts and equal roots; (T-fork-evidence) if two verifiers hold checkpoints with equal sequence and unequal roots both validly signed by the writer key, then the pair constitutes a producer-attributable equivocation proof.
